reason: While the text includes one significant episode of antagonism in the golden calf incident (Exodus 32), where the people reject their leader Moses and demand new gods after his extended absence, this does not characterize the people's general attitude throughout the passage. The predominant pattern shows the people being cooperative and compliant with their leader. Multiple times they affirm 'All that the Lord has spoken we will do' (Exodus 19:8, 24:3, 24:7). When Moses is present, they demonstrate respect and willingness to follow him, even in fearful circumstances. The antagonism displayed is situational—arising specifically during the 40 days when Moses is absent on Mount Sinai—rather than a characteristic trait of the people throughout the narrative.
